projects.name: SPOT
projects.oneLiner: PyTorch library for Stokes IQUV spectral synthesis and inversion, with a pretrained neural-operator solver.
projects.summary: A Python/PyTorch library that implements LTE line-formation physics — opacity, Zeeman line profiles and radiative-transfer solvers — to synthesise Stokes I, Q, U, V for arbitrary atmosphere models, vectorised over batches on CPU or CUDA. Inversion comes in three interchangeable forms: node-parameterised Levenberg–Marquardt with damped SVD, derivative-free CMA-ES for initial-guess search, and a pretrained neural operator (FNO + Transformer + DeepONet-style decoder) that inverts Hinode SP profiles in a single call. The shipped default chains the network guess into a four-cycle node LM run, reaching χ² ≈ 0.05–0.06 on the Hinode SP test case in about 130 s.
highlights: Forward synthesis of Stokes IQUV for arbitrary atmospheres, line lists and wavelength grids, batched on CPU or CUDA
Response functions dI/dx via autograd, finite differences or analytic chain rule; the default `fast` method is exact and cheap
Three inversion routes: node-parameterised LM (damped SVD), batched CMA-ES, and neural-operator network inversion
Default flow (network guess → 4-cycle node LM) reaches χ² ≈ 0.05–0.06 in ~130 s versus ~2500 s for the traditional preset-guess flow
Bundles preset atmospheres (hot11, cool11, falc11, hsra11, …), a line list, and the hinode_sp v3 network trained on 2.36M BIFROST atmospheres
projects.usage: pip install -e . , then `Inversion().invert(wavs, ltau, target)` — defaults already pick the network guess plus four LM cycles.

projects.name: CuSP
projects.oneLiner: GPU-batched Milne–Eddington inversion of solar Stokes profiles with gradient-bias annealing and a physics-informed network.
projects.summary: A PyTorch toolkit for Milne–Eddington inversion of solar spectropolarimetric data, built on a fully differentiable, vectorised Unno–Rachkovsky forward model of the Stokes vector IQUV. It ships four interchangeable batched inversions — CMA-ES, gradient-bias annealing, Levenberg–Marquardt and conjugate SA — plus fast Voigt and Faraday–Voigt profiles from a rational approximation of the Faddeeva function, so no numerical quadrature is needed. A shipped PI2NN network supplies SDO/HMI Fe I 6173 Å initial guesses, letting inversion start from a learned estimate rather than random noise; the code accompanies Chen et al., A&A 710, A227 (2026).
highlights: Fully differentiable, vectorised ME forward synthesis of Stokes IQUV on CPU or CUDA
Four batched inversion methods: CMA-ES (default), gradient-bias annealing (the paper's GBA), Levenberg–Marquardt, conjugate SA
Vectorised response functions give the LM Jacobian in one backward pass per Stokes component, independent of wavelength sampling
Fast Voigt / Faraday–Voigt profiles from a 7/7 complex rational approximation of the Faddeeva function
Shipped PI2NN initial-guess network for SDO/HMI Fe I 6173 Å spectra, selectable as `initial_guess="sdo_hmi"`
projects.usage: pip install -e . , then `MEInversion(wavebands, …)` and call it on continuum-normalised IQUV, optionally with `initial_guess="sdo_hmi"`.

projects.name: arxiv-checkup
projects.oneLiner: Agent skill that watches chosen arXiv categories and files relevant new papers into a three-level Zotero tree.
projects.summary: An agent skill (SKILL.md) that incrementally queries arXiv by category and submission-date window, screens each new title and abstract against the user's stated research areas, and files the relevant ones into Zotero. Entries land in a three-level collection tree — research topic / YYYYMM / first author — and carry an `arxiv:<id>` tag for deduplication and provenance. A state file records `lastRun` and the set of seen IDs, so consecutive runs neither repeat papers nor miss the month boundary.
highlights: Configurable arXiv group → archive → category selection instead of a hard-wired field
AI abstract screening against free-text research areas, which also names the topic collection
Creates the Zotero tree as `[root] / topic / YYYYMM / author` and tags items `arxiv:<id>`
Incremental state (lastRun + seen IDs) with a one-day lookback buffer for arXiv indexing lag
Zero-dependency Node ≥ 22 scripts with a bundled offline taxonomy.json
projects.usage: Install into a skills directory and ask the agent to run a checkup, or drive `scripts/arxiv.mjs` and `scripts/zotero.mjs` directly.

projects.name: dsh-overleaf
projects.oneLiner: Overleaf workbench embedded as a fourth session tab in DeepSeek Harness Web, with selection quoting and caret insertion.
projects.summary: A DeepSeek Harness Web plugin that adds an Overleaf tab beside Chat / Trajectory / Context, loading overleaf.com or a self-hosted instance through a same-origin reverse proxy running inside the DSH host process. Overleaf sends X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors, so a plain iframe is refused; the proxy strips those headers and rebases links so the editor, compiler and PDF preview stay fully operable beneath the native composer. Sharing one origin also makes browser-level bridges possible — text selections flow out as structured quotes and generated LaTeX is written back at the editor caret.
highlights: Same-origin HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy locked to one configured upstream — no open SSRF surface
Full Overleaf editing, compiling and PDF preview inside a session tab, with the DSH composer untouched
Selection quoting through DSH's reference pipeline, plus agent output inserted at the CodeMirror caret after review
Assist panel with AI insert, reviewed selection rewrite, compile-log fixes and outline navigation
Bidirectional .tex and .bib sync guarded by document-ID, revision, snapshot and save-event checks
projects.usage: dsh plugin --profile web add github:gychen-NJU/dsh-overleaf , then restart the web service once.

projects.name: zotnote
projects.oneLiner: Agent skill that turns Zotero PDFs into illustrated Markdown reading notes mirrored into an Obsidian vault.
projects.summary: An agent skill that takes a Zotero item, resolves its PDF (local storage first, Web API as fallback), and extracts both the section structure and every figure and table together with its caption. It then writes a section-by-section Markdown reading note with YAML frontmatter, placing each figure under the section it belongs to, and mirrors the Zotero collection tree into an Obsidian vault so the notes join the knowledge graph. Sections are detected by font-size clustering combined with numbering and heading-vocabulary tests, and figures are located from caption-anchored bounding boxes.
highlights: Section detection by font-size clustering plus numbering pattern and heading vocabulary, filtering false headings
Caption-aware figure and table extraction: embedded bitmaps, vector bounding boxes, and a manual `crop` fallback
Figures are mapped to their section by PDF page, so the explanation sits under the right subsection
Obsidian output mirrors the Zotero collection path, with zotero://select and web links in the frontmatter
Batch mode walks a whole collection and skips notes that already exist, making runs idempotent and resumable
projects.usage: node scripts/run.mjs --key <ZOTERO-KEY> for one paper, or scripts/batch.mjs --collection <name> --recursive for a whole library folder.

projects.name: PF2nlfff
projects.oneLiner: Physics-reinforced GAN that extrapolates a photospheric boundary into a 3D nonlinear force-free magnetic field.
projects.summary: Code for the PF2nlfff projection: given a three-component photospheric boundary field, it runs potential-field extrapolation and a fast reconstruction, then — when a training config is supplied — retrains a physics-reinforced GAN that enforces divergence-free and force-free consistency across the reconstructed volume. The method is presented in the accompanying ApJ paper, and the potential, fast and network fields are returned side by side for comparison. An optional extra renders the resulting 3D field as volume images.
highlights: Potential, rapid and physics-reinforced neural extrapolation in one pipeline call
Physics losses for divergence-free (L_div), force-free (L_ff) and longitudinal-field consistency, with a configurable schedule
Accepts any user-supplied (3, nx, ny) boundary array, not only the bundled Lou & Low test model
Returns three fields side by side — `res.PF`, `res.fast`, `res.nn` — for direct comparison
Optional `[visual]` extra renders 3D volume images; archived on Zenodo with a DOI
projects.usage: pip install . , then `PROGAN(bound_tensor, device="cuda:1")(nz=…)`; omit nn_config to skip the neural retraining stage.
